heroHeadline: Pakistan Says "Time Has Come" to Implement Mecca Pact After Deadly Taif Drone Strike — But Turkey's Ratification Still Stalled Until October
heroSubtitle: A Houthi drone intercepted near Taif on Sep 17 killed one person and wounded two, while Saudi retaliatory strikes on Yemeni telecom towers left four more dead; Houthi leader Abdel-Malik al-Houthi denied the group had targeted Mecca a day earlier, calling the claim "a heinous lie." Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Asif then declared "the time has come" to implement the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, saying "the Mecca agreement applies to us, and we will fulfil our duty" — a marked shift from his Sep 11 framing of the pact as merely "hypothetical." But the shift looks more rhetorical than operational: Turkey has not yet submitted the pact for parliamentary ratification, with approval unlikely before October, Pakistan's own domestic process remains incomplete, and Saudi Arabia has made no formal activation request. Israeli analyst Yoel Guzansky called the partners' muted response "a catastrophe from the Saudi perspective."
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
